title: The Office - Small Talk Series - Showing Interest

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
My name is Marco.
My name is Kathryn and today we're talking about a very, very important part of conversations in English.
segments.zh: 我的名字是 Kathryn，今天我们正在谈论英语对话中非常非常重要的部分。

segments.en: That's right.
Today we are introducing a new series all about small talk.
segments.zh: 今天我们将推出一个关于闲聊的新系列。

segments.en: Okay, what is small talk, Marco?
Well, small talk is just everyday conversation about maybe the weather, about how you are, what's new in your life, etc. just plain conversation.
segments.zh: 好吧，闲聊只是关于天气、你的情况、生活中的新事物等的日常对话。只是简单的对话。

segments.en: So something very simple and usually pretty quick.
segments.zh: 所以非常简单的东西，通常很快。

segments.en: It's what you say to people when you bump into them or when you see them at a party.
segments.zh: 当你碰到他们或在聚会上看到他们时，这就是你对他们说的话。

segments.en: So let's take a listen to today's dialogue and find out just what kind of small talk we have.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听听今天的对话，找出我们有什么样的闲聊。

segments.en: Hey Michelle, this is my friend James.
segments.zh: 嘿，米歇尔，这是我的朋友詹姆斯。

segments.en: He's visiting Shanghai from New York.
Oh, hi James.
Nice to meet you.
So are you visiting for business or pleasure?
segments.zh: 那么你是为了商务还是休闲而来？

segments.en: Well, actually a little of both.
segments.zh: 好吧，实际上两者兼而有之。

segments.en: I'm meeting some business contacts but I'm also taking some Mandarin classes too.
segments.zh: 我正在与一些商业联系人会面，但我也在参加一些普通话课程。

segments.en: Oh, that's cool.
How's it going?
Well, I'm finding the classes pretty tough actually.
segments.zh: 好吧，我发现这些课程实际上非常艰难。

segments.en: But I'm having a great time in Shanghai.
segments.zh: 但我在上海玩得很开心。

segments.en: It's really an amazing city.
segments.zh: 这真的是一个神奇的城市。

segments.en: It sure is.
Are you staying for long?
Only two weeks, unfortunately.
I wish I could stay longer but...
segments.zh: 我希望我能待得更久，但...

segments.en: Well, listen, if you need someone to show you the sites, then just call me.
segments.zh: 要是你需要有人带你逛逛景点，给我打电话就行。

segments.en: I'm having a little get-together at my new apartment next week.
segments.zh: 下周我要在我的新公寓里聚会。

segments.en: So if you want to drop by then...
That sounds great.
I'd love to.
Let me take down your number, Michelle.
segments.zh: 让我记下你的号码，米歇尔。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
So now let's take a look at a lot of great phrases that we've picked out for you this time on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看我们这次在 Fluency Builder 上为您挑选的很多很棒的短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
All right.
So we've got two Fluency Builders today.
segments.zh: 所以我们今天有两个流利的建设者。

segments.en: So we're going to be exploring a lot of different phrases.
segments.zh: 所以我们将探索许多不同的短语。

segments.en: We've got three now.
The first one is very, very common.
You hear this phrase, nice to meet you.
segments.zh: 你听到这句话，很高兴认识你。

segments.en: Right.
So obviously if you meet someone new, you're introduced by your friend or something, you can just say, hi, nice to meet you.
segments.zh: 所以很明显，如果你遇到一个新人，你是由你的朋友介绍的，你可以说，嗨，很高兴认识你。

segments.en: All right.
So, nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too.
That's what we say afterwards because it sounds very funny if you say it two times.
segments.zh: 这就是我们之后说的，因为如果你说两次，这听起来很有趣。

segments.en: So, hi, it's nice to meet you.
Oh, it's nice to meet you too.
Right, exactly.
So she went on, this girl, Michelle, to ask if he is visiting Shanghai for business or pleasure.
segments.zh: 于是她继续说，这个女孩，米歇尔，问他是来上海是为了商务还是休闲。

segments.en: All right.
This is an important difference, something that we often talk about in Small Talk.
segments.zh: 这是一个重要的区别，我们经常在闲聊中谈论的事情。

segments.en: You can travel for business.
That means business trips.
Or you can travel to see different sites and have fun.
segments.zh: 或者您可以前往不同的网站并获得乐趣。

segments.en: That's called pleasure.
And so we often hear this phrase, business or pleasure.
segments.zh: 所以我们经常听到这句话，生意或乐趣。

segments.en: Right.
So if someone comes to your country, you say, oh, so are you here for business or pleasure?
segments.zh: 所以如果有人来你的国家，你说，哦，那么你是来这里是为了生意还是为了娱乐？

segments.en: Oh, I'm here on business or I'm here to see the sites.
segments.zh: 哦，我在这里出差，或者我是来这里查看网站的。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
And so, James is actually in Shanghai doing both things.
segments.zh: 所以，詹姆斯实际上在上海做这两件事。

segments.en: He's on a business trip, but he's also taking Mandarin classes.
segments.zh: 他在出差，但他也在上普通话课。

segments.en: And so Michelle went on to say, that's great.
segments.zh: 所以米歇尔接着说，这太棒了。

segments.en: How's it going?
All right.
You're going to hear this all the time in English.
segments.zh: 你会一直用英语听到这个。

segments.en: We say, how's it going to our friends and family?
segments.zh: 我们说，我们的朋友和家人怎么样？

segments.en: I wouldn't say it in a formal occasion with my boss or with my teacher, but it's very casual, very informal.
segments.zh: 我不会在与我的老板或老师的正式场合说出来，但它非常随意，非常随意。

segments.en: And it's a way to ask how things are.
segments.zh: 这是一种询问情况如何的方式。

segments.en: So you're taking classes.
How's it going?
Exactly.
So this basically means how are the classes going?
segments.zh: 所以这基本上意味着课程进展如何？

segments.en: How is everything?
Right.
Or you could say, oh, Marco, I haven't seen you in a while.
segments.zh: 或者你可以说，哦，马可，我有一段时间没见到你了。

segments.en: How is it going?
And that's another way of saying hi to someone or saying, how are you?
segments.zh: 这是向某人打招呼或说，你好吗？

segments.en: How are you?
How have you been recently?
So there are two differences in that phrase there.
In this case, Michelle is asking how the Mandarin classes are going.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，Michelle 正在询问普通话课程的进展情况。

segments.en: How is it?
Is it good?
Is it bad?
Is it difficult?
Is it easy?
Etc.
But if you say to someone, hi, I haven't seen you for such a long time.
segments.zh: 但如果你对某人说，嗨，我已经很久没有见到你了。

segments.en: How's it going?
That's more of a how are you type thing.
segments.zh: 这更像是你如何打字的东西。

segments.en: That's like how's your life going?
segments.zh: 就像你的生活过得怎么样？

segments.en: Exactly.
So just think about what you're talking about.
Are you talking about general situations like a person's life?
segments.zh: 你是在谈论一个人的生活等一般情况吗？

segments.en: Or are you talking about maybe lessons or class or job?
segments.zh: 或者你说的可能是课程、课堂或工作？

segments.en: That's right.
Okay, so we're going to take a break here.
segments.zh: 好的，我们要在这里休息一下。

segments.en: Let's listen to the dialogue again and we'll be back in a little bit with more phrases.
segments.zh: 让我们再听一次对话，我们会稍微用更多的短语回来。

segments.en: Hey Michelle, this is my friend James.
segments.zh: 嘿，米歇尔，这是我的朋友詹姆斯。

segments.en: He's visiting Shanghai from New York.
Oh, hi James.
Nice to meet you.
So are you visiting for business or pleasure?
segments.zh: 那么你是为了商务还是休闲而来？

segments.en: Well, actually a little of both.
segments.zh: 好吧，实际上两者兼而有之。

segments.en: I'm meeting some business contacts, but I'm also taking some Mandarin classes too.
segments.zh: 我正在与一些商业联系人会面，但我也在参加一些普通话课程。

segments.en: Oh, that's cool.
How's it going?
Well, I'm finding the classes pretty tough actually, but I'm having a great time in Shanghai.
segments.zh: 好吧，我发现这些课程非常艰难，但我在上海玩得很开心。

segments.en: It's really an amazing city.
segments.zh: 这真的是一个神奇的城市。

segments.en: It sure is.
Are you staying for long?
Only two weeks, unfortunately.
I wish I could stay longer, but...
segments.zh: 我希望我能待得更久，但是...

segments.en: Well, listen, if you need someone to show you the sites, then just call me.
segments.zh: 要是你需要有人带你逛逛景点，给我打电话就行。

segments.en: I'm having a little get together at my new apartment next week.
segments.zh: 下周我要在我的新公寓聚会。

segments.en: So if you want to drop by then...
That sounds great.
I'd love to.
Let me take down your number, Michelle.
segments.zh: 让我记下你的号码，米歇尔。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
So now let's take a look at Fluency Builder Part Two.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看 Fluency Builder 的第二部分。

segments.en: So Michelle, at the end of today's dialogue says, if you need someone to show you the sites, then just call me.
segments.zh: 所以米歇尔，在今天的对话结束时说，如果你需要有人给你看网站，那就给我打电话。

segments.en: All right.
So to show someone the sites, we talked about this a little bit earlier with that word pleasure.
segments.zh: 因此，为了向某人展示这些网站，我们更早地讨论了这个词，这个词很高兴。

segments.en: What does it mean to show someone the sites, Marco?
segments.zh: 向某人展示网站意味着什么，马可？

segments.en: So basically, the sites, we're talking about the different attractions of a city or place.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，这些网站，我们谈论的是城市或地方的不同景点。

segments.en: So the museums, maybe different buildings or different attractions in general.
segments.zh: 所以博物馆，也许是不同的建筑或不同的景点。

segments.en: What is there to sightsee?
Okay, so we are in Paris, Marco, and I say, hey, I'd love to show you the sites.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们在巴黎，马可，我说，嘿，我很想向您展示这些网站。

segments.en: What do you expect to see?
So maybe we would go to the Eiffel Tower.
segments.zh: 所以也许我们会去埃菲尔铁塔。

segments.en: Maybe we would go to...
Notre Dame Cathedral.
Exactly.
And we would go see all these different sites and that would mean that you are showing me the sites.
segments.zh: 我们会去看看所有这些不同的网站，这意味着你正在向我展示这些网站。

segments.en: You are taking me to see all these sites.
segments.zh: 你带我去看所有这些网站。

segments.en: And she is also having a little get together at her apartment, at her new apartment.
segments.zh: 她还在她的新公寓，在她的公寓里聚会。

segments.en: So what is a little get together?
This is a noun.
This is a get together.
So think about this.
Two different words actually, get together, but it's a noun, it's a thing.
segments.zh: 实际上有两个不同的词，聚在一起，但它是一个名词，它是一个东西。

segments.en: It's like a party, but it's a small party.
segments.zh: 这就像一个派对，但它是一个小聚会。

segments.en: Right.
A little get together.
So I just, I like to think of a get together as something very casual, something very small, sometimes intimate, where you just have three or four or five friends.
segments.zh: 所以我只是，我喜欢把聚会想象成一种非常随意的东西，一些非常小的东西，有时是亲密的，你只有三四个或五个朋友。

segments.en: And it's, yeah, it's not as big as a party where everyone's dancing.
segments.zh: 它是，是的，它没有每个人都在跳舞的派对。

segments.en: Okay.
So a little get together is just a small group of people, you invite them over to your house, very relaxed, very casual.
segments.zh: 所以一点点聚会只是一小群人，你邀请他们到你家，很放松，很随意。

segments.en: It's not really a party.
It's more of a reunion of friends.
And like we said, it's a noun.
segments.zh: 就像我们说的，它是一个名词。

segments.en: So you say, I'm having a get together, you should come.
segments.zh: 所以你说，我要聚在一起，你应该来。

segments.en: Okay.
And she actually asks them to come, but she says it in a different way.
segments.zh: 她实际上要求他们来，但她以不同的方式说。

segments.en: She says, if you want to drop by.
segments.zh: 她说，如果你想过来的话。

segments.en: Okay.
This is something people often say in small talk, because you don't want to say, you should come stay for a while because that's, I don't know, they just met.
segments.zh: 这是人们在闲聊中经常说的话，因为你不想说，你应该来呆一会儿，因为那是，我不知道，他们刚刚认识。

segments.en: It's not in order.
Yeah.
So you should drop by means you should come and see and decide if you want to stay.
segments.zh: 所以你应该放弃的意思是你应该来看看并决定你是否想留下来。

segments.en: So basically it's also kind of a relaxed way of saying you can come whenever you want during the, during our party or our get together.
segments.zh: 所以基本上这也是一种轻松的说法，你可以在我们聚会期间或聚会期间随时来。

segments.en: So if the get together is 9pm to midnight, you can drop by whenever, 10 o'clock, 11 o'clock.
segments.zh: 因此，如果聚会是晚上 9 点到午夜，您可以随时来，10 点钟，11 点钟。

segments.en: So to drop by is to come for a short period.
segments.zh: 所以顺便过来就是短暂的到来。

segments.en: So if we're talking on the phone and I say, I'll drop by your house later on today, that means I'm going to go to your house very quickly at an unexpected time.
segments.zh: 所以如果我们在打电话，我说，我今天晚些时候会去你家，这意味着我会在意想不到的时间很快去你家。

segments.en: Yeah.
Or you could use it in a question, you know, Marco, I really wanted to borrow that DVD.
segments.zh: 或者你可以在一个问题中使用它，你知道，Marco，我真的很想借那张 DVD。

segments.en: When can I drop by to pick it up?
segments.zh: 我什么时候可以顺路取货？

segments.en: Okay.
Very, very good.
So let's take a look at our last phrase.
segments.zh: 所以让我们来看看我们的最后一句话。

segments.en: Michelle and James decided that they want to keep in touch and so he said, let me take down your number.
segments.zh: 米歇尔和詹姆斯决定他们要保持联系，所以他说，让我记下你的电话号码。

segments.en: Okay.
So we're not talking about taking it anywhere, taking a number anywhere and going somewhere.
segments.zh: 所以我们不是在谈论把它带到任何地方，在任何地方拿一个数字然后去某个地方。

segments.en: We're talking about writing something down.
segments.zh: 我们正在谈论写下一些东西。

segments.en: So in this case, your number is your phone number.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，您的号码就是您的电话号码。

segments.en: Okay.
Let me take down your number means let me write down your telephone number.
segments.zh: 让我记下你的号码意味着让我写下你的电话号码。

segments.en: Uh huh.
Okay.
So it's another way of saying, let me write down your telephone number.
segments.zh: 所以这是另一种说法，让我写下你的电话号码。

segments.en: Take down my phone number.
Call me later.
That's right.
So can I take down your number so I can call you later?
segments.zh: 那么我可以记下你的号码，以便以后给你打电话吗？

segments.en: Okay.
That's another way of asking this question.
segments.zh: 这是问这个问题的另一种方式。

segments.en: Very good.
All right.
